newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin reported improving, foes plot his removal.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin reported improving, foes plot his removal.

text.p: Russian doctors said on Tuesday President Boris Yeltsin's condition was improving in hospital, hours after political foes began looking at ways to oust him on health grounds.

The lower house of parliament's security committee, which is headed by a senior member of the opposition Communist Party, urged the chamber to discuss removing Yeltsin. Its appeal will go to legal experts for consideration.
But the Kremlin later said the doctors had noticed a considerable improvement in Yeltsin, who has been in an elite Moscow hospital with pneumonia for almost a week.
"His (Yeltsin's) condition has improved considerably, he is more physically active," the presidential press service said. "There is only sporadic wheeziness in his lungs."

The president, who turns 66 on February 1, also held his first meeting since he fell ill with anyone other than his doctors and family. The presidential press service said he had 40 minutes of talks at the hospital with the chief of his Kremlin staff, Anatoly Chubais.
The Kremlin said they had discussed the general political situation and personnel matters.
The doctors' report appeared to point to the biggest improvement in Yeltsin's condition since he was admitted to the Central Clinical Hospital on January 8.

Kremlin statements in the last few days had said either that the president's condition was stable or that there had been no breakthrough in tackling his pneumonia. A top Kremlin doctor has said the inflammation had affected both lungs.
But there was still no indication when the president, who had heart surgery on November 5 and did not return to work in the Kremlin until December 23, would leave hospital.
Yeltsin's political opponents, questioning his ability to rule the vast country of 150 million people, began moves that could develop into a bid to remove him.

The security committee in the State Duma, the lower house, called on the chamber to declare "the premature cessation of Yeltsin's powers due to his persistent incapacity, through the state of his health, to carry out the duties of president of the Russian Federation".
It said that, under the constitution, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin should stand in for three months while a new presidential election was organised.

Communist Gennady Seleznyov, the Duma chairman, said constitutional provisions to oust the president on health grounds were "very hazy". He doubted whether the attempt to remove Yeltsin would succeed.

The motion will be discussed by the Duma's legal department and then by party groups in parliament. Although the motion has little chance of success, the discussions could throw some light on the vague constitutional position on presidential illness.

Two presidential hopefuls, sacked national security adviser Alexander Lebed and Communist Party leader Gennady Zyuganov, have urged Yeltsin to step down. Other officials want changes in the constitution, which gives the president huge powers.
The Kremlin said in a statement that speculation about Yeltsin's health would come to nothing. It said the president had dismissed the need for constitutional changes.
